SUBJECT: Sclerorhynchiformes, four different extinct sawskates: Sclerorhynchus atavus, Libanopristis hiram, Onchopristis numida, and Ischyrhiza mira. Use conservative whole-animal reconstructions. All must have ray-like flattened bodies, pectoral fins joined to head, paired pelvic fins, muscular tails with small dorsal fins and caudal fin, eyes on top and a long flat rostrum with lateral denticles. Four distinct silhouettes in loosely arranged two-by-two composition, with snouts and tails oriented so they fit without crossing. Sclerorhynchus in olive grey dorsolateral view, slender rostrum with relatively small pointed denticles; Libanopristis in warm sandy brown dorsal view with long narrow rostrum and small closely spaced lateral denticles; Onchopristis robust charcoal-brown dorsolateral view, long rostrum with distinctly larger hook-bearing lateral denticles (each crown has a small backward barb); Ischyrhiza muted slate grey with pointed blade-like unbarbed rostral denticles. Subtle natural variation in patterns and viewing angle, no invented extreme fins. Distinguish them by rostral denticles and credible proportions, not fantastical ornament. No modern sawfish, sawsharks, manta rays, oral tooth illustrations or fossil fragments. Avoid shark-shaped free pectorals and ventral-view mouths on dorsal surfaces.
